ative flange increases (with thinner flange naturally should have higher array efficiency):: Ta(C) Figure 3.15 illustrates the relationship of the resolved intensity at 600 nm on a medium and long time scale when the ambient temperature is varied. In the initial condition representing the earliest stage of surface phase change, Ta solution is expected to have a higher value. However, as this phase change progresses and the temperature reaches about 18 0C, the higher value begins to decrease rapidly due to increasing absorbed power profile, thereby lowering the accumulation rate of radiating concentrated liquid elements on the Ni surface layer, leading to the resolution appearing to be quasi absent.

Figure 3.15: Temperature dependence of the intensity at 600 nm; observed with midnew spectrum of Ta solution.

Figure 3.16: Illumination time dependence of the intensity at 600 nm; observed with midnew spectrum of Ta solution.

Figure 3.17: Illumination time dependence of the intensity at 600 nm; observed with midnew spectrum of Ta solution.

Figure 3.18 shows the relationship between Ta solution temperature and the absorbed power profile in the sub-area where incident light is limited. When the Ta solution absorbed power is minimized at 18 0C, the heat transfer inside the Ta solution becomes nearly impossible, and the peak value measured with 1 milliwatt of incident light will not change, but the effective area within the analyzer will decrease by 15 times smaller by enlarging the mass impact area on the Ni(II) surface by the elevated Ta concentration on the interface.
